hints: Two passes work: count the length, then walk to the node before the target.
For one pass: if one pointer starts n nodes ahead of another, where is the trailing one when the leader reaches the end?
Start both at a dummy node before the head so removing the head needs no special case.

insight.oneLiner: Advance `right` n steps, then move both until `right` is None; `left` is just before the target.
insight.pattern: Gap of n between two pointers

recall.a: left at a dummy before head, right at head; then right moves n steps.
recall.q: Where do left and right start?

recall.a: When n equals the length, the head is removed - the dummy is its predecessor.

signals: one pass over a singly linked list
insight.why: Keeping a constant gap converts 'n-th from the end' into a position you can reach in one pass. The dummy node gives the head a predecessor.

oneLiner: Advance `right` n steps, then move both until `right` is None; `left` is just before the target.

pitfalls.explain: When n equals the list length, the head itself goes. A dummy node before the head handles it.
pitfalls.title: Crashed when removing the head

pitfalls.explain: Check the gap: after moving right n steps from head (with left at the dummy), left stops just before the target.
pitfalls.title: Removed the wrong node

solutions.idea: Find the length first, then walk to the node before the target.
solutions.name: Count, then remove

footnotes.text: The gap between left and right never changes. When right falls off the end, left sits exactly one node before the n-th node from the end.

solutions.idea: Keep a gap of n nodes between two pointers so the trailing one stops right before the target.
solutions.name: Two pointers with a gap

statement:
Given the `head` of a linked list, remove the **`n`-th node counting from the end** and return the head of the resulting list.

Follow-up: can you do it in one pass?
title: Remove Nth Node From End of List
